record.original_question: Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic in D_mu^s(M) starting at the identity, and decide whether the existence of conjugate points is related to Arnold's stability criterion for stationary flows.

evidence.quote: Problem 19. (a) Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any L2 geodesic starting from the identity in Dµs (M ). (b) Is there a relation between existence of conjugate points in Dµs (M ) and Arnold stability criterion for stationary flows in M ? The answer to (a) may have some bearing on Problem 8. For example, if the order of any conjugate point turns out to be always greater than one then the fact that the exponential map is Fredholm of index zero would indicate that there is only one connected component of the identity over which expe is a covering map, see [100]. Regarding (b) recall that according to Arnold’s criterion [2, 5, 6] a stationary flow of an ideal fluid is Lyapunov stable if the quadratic form given by the second derivative of the kinetic energy restricted to the coadjoint orbits is positive or negative definite. It can be shown that for simple domains such as the disk, the annulus and the straight channel no steady flows satisfying Arnold’s stability possess conjugate points. (We assume here that the two-dimensional fluid domain M has a nonempty boundary.) It is therefore tempting to expect that this is true more generally. See [33] for additional background and [137] for recent results in this direction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with (possibly nonempty) boundary, and let $D^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of Sobolev-class $H^s$ (with $s > \dim M/2 + 1$) volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric whose geodesics through the identity correspond to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations. Given an $L^2$ geodesic $\eta(t)$ in $D^s_\mu(M)$ with $\eta(0)=\mathrm{id}$, a point $\eta(t_0)$ is called a conjugate point along $\eta$ if the differential of the Riemannian exponential map $\exp_e$ at $t_0\dot\eta(0)$ fails to be a linear isomorphism; its order is the dimension of the kernel of $d\exp_e$ at that point (with appropriate notions of mono- and epi-conjugacy in the infinite-dimensional setting).

(a) Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any $L^2$ geodesic in $D^s_\mu(M)$ starting at the identity. In particular, decide whether this order is always strictly greater than one.

(b) A stationary flow of an ideal fluid on $M$ is Arnold (Lyapunov) stable if the quadratic form given by the second derivative of the kinetic energy, restricted to the coadjoint orbit of the corresponding vorticity, is either positive definite or negative definite. Determine whether the existence of conjugate points along the $L^2$ geodesic in $D^s_\mu(M)$ generated by a stationary flow is related to the failure of Arnold's stability criterion for that flow; in particular, decide whether every Arnold-stable stationary flow on $M$ generates a geodesic with no conjugate points.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known but the general questions remain open. Preston (2006) showed that on the volumorphism group the differential of the exponential map at a first conjugate point is never Fredholm, and conjugate points must be either epiconjugate-but-not-monoconjugate or monoconjugate of infinite order, yet the precise order along a general L2 geodesic is not determined. For part (b), non-existence of conjugate points has been verified along Arnold-stable steady states on simple two-dimensional domains (disk, annulus, channel), and the Misiołek curvature criterion provides a sufficient condition, but a general equivalence/relationship between Arnold stability and absence of conjugate points has not been established.

status_evidence.title: On the Volumorphism Group, the First Conjugate Point is Always the Hardest
status_evidence.snippet: At a first conjugate point along a geodesic in the volumorphism group, the differential of the exponential map always fails to be Fredholm.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results on the order of the first conjugate point exist, but the precise order remains undetermined in general.

status_evidence.title: Conjugate and cut points in ideal fluid motion
status_evidence.snippet: Non-existence of conjugate points along Arnold stable steady states on the annulus, disk and channel.
status_evidence.claim: Relation between Arnold stability and absence of conjugate points is established for simple 2D domains but open in general.

status_evidence.title: The WKB Method for Conjugate Points in the Volumorphism Group
status_evidence.snippet: Conjugate points in the volumorphism group are either epiconjugate-not-monoconjugate or monoconjugate of infinite order.
status_evidence.claim: Order behavior is constrained but not pinned down for all geodesics.
